metadata.criterion: Can select keyed answer from printed teaching/illustration and ordinary application. Does not mean every clause of a keyed answer or every distractor explanation is taught.

status_definitions.covered: Printed teaching/illustration supplies keyed-answer selection or required principle/formula; retained rounding qualifications apply.
status_definitions.not_covered: Exact required illustration or knowledge missing.
status_definitions.prompt_only: Supplied numbers/formulas permit arithmetic, but the book does not teach this method/model.

metadata.page_numbering: One-based physical PDF pages including cover; continuous printed folios and PDF labels verified in H6. Original bank page field is unrelated.
metadata.method: Fresh extraction of all 578 pages. All 178 retained scenario decisions checked against exactly preserved teaching bodies and remapped anchors/guards, retaining 55 target decisions and 68 claim links. All 616 sign questions matched to exact illustrated caption units and hashed asset placements. All 206 numerical instances recalculated from prompt inputs; new stopping/fuel calculations use Decimal. Four fuel midpoint keys remain qualified by printed rounding disclosure. External links, lookup and bibliography are not teaching evidence.

status_definitions.covered: Printed teaching/illustration supplies keyed-answer selection or required principle/formula.

metadata.method: All 178 scenarios reviewed against fresh revised page bodies; all 55 target teaching anchors and 68 essential source-linked claims checked. All 616 sign records matched by exact illustrated code and verified asset placement, excluding code-only lookup/bibliography. scenario_pages.50:
KörkortGo · M03-L02
M03-L02
Combine the instructions
Your goal: Interpret signs, panels, markings and signals together, including authorised
directions.
Requirements. Follow the traffic instructions that apply to you. Where an instruction differs from
a general traffic rule, the instruction governs. A steady traffic-light indication takes precedence
over a yield or stop sign; a police officer's direction takes precedence over the rules and ordinary
traffic instructions. This is not a rule that a green signal cancels every other restriction.
Authorised guards also give traffic directions that must be followed. Traffic Regulation, chapter 2
§§2–4
Authorised directions
Separate examples. A static picture does not show the complete movement; read the description and the official
instruction.
P1 · Police stop instruction — front and rear
Stopp
Traffic approaching the officer from the front or rear must
stop; traffic approaching from the sides may proceed. The
officer's continuing orientation matters even after the arm
movement. Officer faces the viewer with one arm extended
sideways.
Transportstyrelsen · official description
scenario_pages.44:
KörkortGo · M03-L01 · Continued
Continue the learning
Family
What to establish
A useful driving question
A — warning
The nature of a hazard ahead
What might be hidden, and how much
space do I need?
B — priority
A duty or relationship at a
conflict point
Must I yield or stop, and to whom?
C — prohibition/restriction
What movement, vehicle or limit
is restricted
Does this apply to my vehicle and journey?
D — mandatory instruction
The required route, side or
permitted traffic
Which path must I take?
E — instruction
A road or area with a particular
meaning or regime
Which rules begin or end here?
These are learning questions, not substitutes for the individual sign descriptions. A warning of
children, for example, does not assign a new numerical speed by itself; your speed must still
allow safe control and a response to foreseeable hazards. A posted maximum speed is a ceiling,
not a demand to maintain that speed. Road Signs Regulation, chapter 2 · Traffic Regulation,
chapter 3 §§14–15
Requirements. B1 means yield to vehicles on the crossing road or route. Make that intention
clear early and proceed only without danger or obstruction. B2 requires a stop before entering
the crossing road or track area. Stop at the stop line; without one, stop immediately before the
signal or before entering the crossing road or track area, as applicable. A rolling pause does not
meet a stop duty. Road Signs Regulation, B1–B2 · Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §§5 and 19
scenario_pages.97:
KörkortGo · M04-L01 · Continued
Continue the learning
T15 · Priority-road layout at the junction
Vägars fortsättning i korsning
Traffic on the thin-line roads yields to traffic on the thick-line
road. Follow the actual road layout shown. Thick road
connects the top and right edges; thin branches extend down
and left.
Transportstyrelsen · official description
T15-2 · Priority-road layout at the junction
Vägars fortsättning i korsning
Traffic on the thin-line roads yields to traffic on the thick-line
road. Follow the actual road layout shown. Thick road
connects the top and left edges; thin branches extend down
and right.
Transportstyrelsen · official description
Different duties apply when entering a road from premises, a car park, fuel station, similar
roadside area, path or similar exit, or from terrain, a pedestrian street, walking-speed area or
cycle street. After crossing a footway or cycle path to enter a road, the exit provision also
matters. Do not decide solely from a kerb's appearance; identify the actual layout. Joining a
priority road without an acceleration lane generally requires yielding, subject to the provision for
joining without changing lane. Roundabout entry has its own duty. Traffic Regulation, chapter 3
§§21–23
To yield, show your intention by reducing speed or stopping in good time. Only continue when
the other road user's position, distance and speed allow movement without danger or
obstruction. A stop duty requires a complete stop even if the road appears empty. Traffic
Regulation, chapter 3 §§5 and 19
scenario_pages.102:
KörkortGo · M04-L01 · Illustration
Where a stop is required
Stop duty: the teal car approaches the stop line. A complete stop is required at the line. This detail shows the
stopping point, not the whole junction.
scenario_pages.94:
KörkortGo · M04-L01
M04-L01
Decide who goes first
Your goal: Explain junction decisions using priority instructions and right-hand priority,
and recognise special situations.
Requirements. Where two vehicle paths cross, the general rule is to yield to a vehicle
approaching from your right, except where another applicable rule or instruction determines the
relationship. Road width, familiarity or the fact that you are travelling straight does not by itself
establish priority. Right-hand priority can apply at a three-way junction or within a parking area.
Right-hand priority · Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §18
Priority and junction instructions
Independent examples: A29 variants show different branch layouts. Read thick and thin roads on each T15 panel; do
not assume an approach orientation.
A28 · Junction with right-hand priority
Varning för vägkorsning
The junction ahead is governed by the right-hand priority rule.
Do not assume the broader road has priority. Black cross
inside a warning triangle.
Transportstyrelsen · official description
scenario_pages.103:
KörkortGo · M04-L01 · Knowledge check
Check your understanding
Knowledge check. You drive straight on a broad road and another car approaches from the right
on a narrower ordinary road. No signs, signals or special rule apply. Who yields?
Remember: Determine the applicable rule before judging the available gap.
scenario_pages.100:
KörkortGo · M04-L01 · Illustration
Ordinary junction or exit?
Ordinary junction: no signs, signals or special rule
apply. The yellow car approaches from the teal
driver’s right. Road width alone does not determine
priority.
Driveway exit: the teal car is entering across the
footway. Identify the exit duty before choosing a gap.
Worked decision. You approach from a driveway on the right of a car travelling along the road.
You yield under the exit rule. Being on the other driver's right does not displace that duty.
scenario_pages.113:
KörkortGo · M04-L02 · Illustration
Observe the complete turn
Right turn beside a cyclist: the cycling route and receiving road remain open. Check the cyclist’s movement before
crossing the route. No movement arrow grants priority.
Worked decision. A driver signals to move right while a cyclist is beside the vehicle. The driver
waits. Signalling earlier would have helped communication, but it would never have removed
the need to ensure the cyclist's safety.

Ordinary vehicle signals
Red, red/amber, green and amber appear in that order. Flashing amber is a separate condition, not the next stage of
the normal cycle. Arrow indications apply to the direction shown.
SIG1 · Red vehicle signal
Röd
Stop before the stop line or, if none, before the signal. An
outline arrow limits the indication to the direction shown. Red
left arrow, red full lamp and red bicycle signal examples.

Röd + gul

Do not start merely because amber has appeared. Red and
amber illuminated together in arrow, full-lamp and bicycle
examples.
Transportstyrelsen · official description

Grön
You may proceed subject to the remaining traffic duties. A
green arrow applies to its direction, including when another
signal indication appears simultaneously. Green arrow, green

scenario_pages.104:
KörkortGo · M04-L02
M04-L02
Turn with a complete picture
Your goal: Plan observation, signalling, position and margins for turns and lane changes.
Requirements. Before a turn, check that it will not obstruct oncoming traffic or traffic on the
road you are entering. Pay attention to people travelling in the same direction, including those
behind you. Position early: normally the right-hand lane for a right turn and the left-hand lane
for a left turn where multiple approach lanes exist, subject to applicable signs, markings and
space provisions. On a two-way road, a left turn is normally prepared near the road centre; on a
one-way carriageway, near the left edge. Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §§24–29
Choose a permitted direction
Prohibitions, mandatory directions, one-way signs and lane arrows are separate sets. They are not all present at one
fictional junction.
Prohibited movements
C25 · Prohibited turn
Förbud mot sväng i korsning
The depicted turn is prohibited at the relevant junction. A
length panel can extend the restriction across several
junctions. Left-turn arrow crossed out.
Transportstyrelsen · official description
scenario_pages.66:
KörkortGo · M03-L02 · Worked decision
Apply the learning
A green signal and a queue beyond the junction. Opposing traffic is separated and the stop line is before the
crossing road. The scene is illustrative, not to scale.
Worked decision. Your signal is green, but a queue fills the space beyond the junction. Wait
where you will not obstruct crossing traffic rather than entering a space you cannot clear. Traffic
Regulation, chapter 3 §20
Knowledge check. Does amber mean accelerate to beat red?
Remember: Read the whole instruction and the space beyond it.
scenario_pages.139:
KörkortGo · M05-L01 · Continued
Continue the learning
T10 · People with impaired hearing
Nedsatt hörsel
People with impaired hearing commonly use the area. Do not
assume a horn will be heard. Three black dots inside a black
circle on yellow.
Transportstyrelsen · official description
Horses and riders also belong in your traffic assessment. Vehicle rules apply to riding and leading
horses in relevant respects; they are not simply pedestrians because they travel slowly. Give
them an unhurried, spacious interaction, and avoid unnecessary noise. This is a cautious
application of the general duty of care, not a fixed passing-distance rule. Transportstyrelsen:
horses in traffic
Horses and riders
This warning supports early observation. It does not specify a fixed passing distance.
A18 · Horse riders ahead
Varning för ridande
Riders often cross or use this stretch of road. Prepare for an
unhurried, spacious encounter. Horse and rider inside a
warning triangle.
Transportstyrelsen · official description
Bus rule. Where the maximum permitted speed is 50 km/h or lower, a driver approaching a bus
whose driver signals to leave a bus stop must slow and give it the opportunity to leave, stopping
if needed. The bus driver must also take particular care. If passing on the right of a bus or tram
stopped at a stop without a refuge, stop to allow boarding or alighting passengers free passage.
Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §§45 and 58
scenario_pages.141:
KörkortGo · M05-L01 · Share the space
Share the space
Bus comparison · Check the road limit. The threshold concerns the maximum permitted speed
on the road, not how fast you happen to be travelling. At a 70 km/h limit, the special bus-stop
departure rule above does not apply. The bus must wait for an entry that can be made without
danger or unnecessary obstruction. You still have a duty to adapt speed to facilitate an observed
entry into your lane. A bus indicator does not create unconditional priority, and the higher road
limit does not excuse deliberately blocking it. Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §§43–45
Road limit
Duties when the bus signals to leave its stop
50 km/h or lower
Slow and let the bus leave; stop if needed. The bus driver must take
particular care.
70 km/h, ordinary entry into your lane
The special bus-exit duty does not apply. The bus waits for a safe
entry; you adapt speed to facilitate the observed entry.
Safety advice · Let a guide dog work. Do not pet, call to or talk to a working guide dog to attract
its attention. Distraction can endanger the person it is helping. Allow the pair room and time; if
you need to communicate, address the handler rather than trying to direct the dog. The handler
chooses the route and remains in control. For example, a passenger beside your parked car
wants to greet a guide dog at a crossing. Ask them to leave it working and keep the path clear.
MFD: meeting a working guide dog
Traffic terminology · A bicycle is a vehicle. A person riding an ordinary pedal bicycle is operating
a vehicle, even without an engine. “Vehicle” does not mean only “motor vehicle”. Apply the
relevant cyclist duties and protections; crossing distinctions remain in M04-L03.
Transportstyrelsen: bicycle definition
scenario_pages.142:
KörkortGo · M05-L01 · Illustration
Leave room for the bus and people
The bus signals to leave its stop. The full-width middle lane remains separate from the opposing lane. In the worked
decision the road limit is 40 km/h; available road width does not remove the bus duty.
Worked decision. On a 40 km/h street, a bus signals out. You ease speed early and leave room
rather than trying to squeeze past. You also watch for people near the stop; making space for the
bus is not your only task. Compare an otherwise ordinary 70 km/h road: the bus waits for a safe
entry, while you still adapt speed to help an observed entry into your lane. Travelling at 40 on
that 70 road does not activate the special bus rule.

Gul

would be dangerous because you are already too close. An
outline arrow limits the indication to its direction. Amber

Blinkande gul

A red lane-control cross closes the lane; a green downward arrow allows its use; a diagonal

for pedestrians or public transport are not automatically instructions for your car. Road Signs
Regulation, chapter 3 §§7–15
scenario_pages.115:
KörkortGo · M04-L03
M04-L03
Crossings belong to people
Your goal: Distinguish pedestrian crossings, cycle passages and cycle crossings and apply
the relevant duties.
Requirements. At an uncontrolled pedestrian crossing, yield to pedestrians who are on it or
about to enter. Someone walking a bicycle is a pedestrian; someone riding one is not made a
pedestrian merely by using the painted crossing. A person using a wheelchair at walking speed is
covered by pedestrian rules. This distinction never removes the general duty to avoid danger.
Pedestrian crossings · Wheelchair users · Traffic Regulation, chapter 1 §4 and chapter 3 §61
Recognise a pedestrian crossing
The warning identifies an approach. B3 and M15 identify the crossing itself; the mirrored B3 artwork does not
change the duty.
A13 · Pedestrian crossing ahead
Varning för övergångsställe
Prepare to encounter a pedestrian crossing. Identify the
crossing itself and the controls that apply there. Pedestrian on
crossing stripes inside a warning triangle.
Transportstyrelsen · official description
scenario_pages.117:
KörkortGo · M04-L03 · Continued
Continue the learning
Situation
Driver's duty
Uncontrolled cycle passage,
approaching without turning
Adapt speed so cyclists or class II moped riders already on the passage
are not endangered. A rider coming from a cycle path generally has a
yielding duty.
Uncontrolled cycle passage after your
turn or roundabout exit
Travel slowly and allow riders on or about to enter the passage an
opportunity to pass.
Cycle crossing (cykelöverfart)
Yield to cyclists and class II moped riders on it or about to enter it.
A cycle crossing has both markings and the cycle-crossing sign, together with a design that
secures low vehicle speeds. Do not identify it only by painted blocks. Transportstyrelsen: cycle
passages and crossings · Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §§61–61a
Identify a cycle crossing
Separately labelled components. M16 alone does not establish a cycle crossing; read the sign, markings and road
design together.
B8 · Cycle crossing
Cykelöverfart
This identifies a cycle crossing. Drivers yield to cyclists and
class II moped riders on or about to enter it; riders must also
consider approaching vehicles. Cyclist above a crossing in a
blue square.
Transportstyrelsen · official description
M14 · Give-way line
Väjningslinje
This identifies the line drivers should not pass while yielding.
Row of white give-way triangles.
Transportstyrelsen · official description
scenario_pages.121:
KörkortGo · M04-L03 · Illustration
Identify the crossing and your movement
Cycle crossing: B8, the crossing markings and the
raised treatment distinguish this example. Surface
colour alone does not determine the duty.
Passage after a roundabout exit: the cyclist is
approaching the marked passage on the receiving
road. The exit movement matters to the driver’s duty.
Worked decision. You leave a roundabout and reach an uncontrolled cycle passage. A cyclist is
about to enter. You slow and give the rider an opportunity to pass; applying only the
straight-ahead passage rule would miss the significance of your exit.
scenario_pages.123:
KörkortGo · M04-L04
M04-L04
Choose a safe path through a
roundabout
Your goal: Describe an approach, entry and exit plan that accounts for priority, lanes,
signalling and nearby crossings.
Requirements. Travel anticlockwise and yield on entry to vehicles already circulating. Choose an
appropriate lane for the onward route and obey signs and markings. There is no general
requirement to signal solely for entering; signal lane changes and significant sideways
movements, and signal right when leaving. Any lane change must be safe and must not create
unnecessary obstruction. Transportstyrelsen: roundabout guide · Traffic Regulation, chapter 3
§§13, 22, 43 and 65–66
Roundabout instructions
Approach warning, circulation direction, yielding, lane guidance and island marker are distinct instructions. Read
the actual combination on the road.
A30 · Roundabout ahead
Varning för cirkulationsplats
Prepare for a roundabout and identify the entry instructions
before reaching it. Circulating arrows inside a warning triangle.
Transportstyrelsen · official description
scenario_pages.127:
KörkortGo · M04-L04 · Illustration
Check the receiving road
Exit: the teal car approaches a cycle passage. Signal right when leaving and check the passage as a separate conflict.
scenario_pages.125:
KörkortGo · M04-L04 · Continued
Continue the learning
Learning approach. Read the layout before reaching the yield point. Reduce speed enough to
judge circulating traffic and the available space. Observe crossings on the approach as separate
conflicts. Inside, hold your intended path and continue checking nearby vehicles. A large vehicle
may need more room than its apparent lane width suggests. Roundabout guide
Plan the exit early. Moving from an inner lane across an outer lane is a lane change, even though
you call the whole movement “leaving the roundabout.” Do not assume a vehicle beside you will
leave at the same exit. If the exit cannot be taken safely, continue as the layout allows and
re-plan. On leaving, check the crossing area again; the duties in M04-L03 still apply. Roundabout
guide · Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §§60–62
scenario_pages.126:
KörkortGo · M04-L04 · Illustration
Entry and circulation are separate decisions
Approach: B1 and D3 identify the entry instructions.
The teal car approaches the yield point while the
yellow car circulates anticlockwise.
Circulation: two lanes surround the island. The teal car
in the inner lane and yellow car in the outer lane need
separate space; the inner lane confers no exit priority.
Worked decision. Your desired exit is approaching, but a car is alongside in the outer lane. You
do not cut across it. You preserve a safe path and choose another opportunity consistent with
the lane markings. Recovering the route is secondary to avoiding a conflict.

Continue the learning

Other prohibitions cover cycle lanes, hatched areas, roundabouts and lanes reserved for regular
public transport. These examples are not an exhaustive catalogue of local restrictions. Traffic
Regulation, chapter 3 §§47–55

Travel is left to right. No stopping on the crossing or within 10 m before it. Shading shows the rule’s extent, not a
braking distance; the drawing is not to scale.

Other vehicles may stop only for boarding or alighting without obstructing the service. Shading is explanatory, not a

Worked decision. It is an ordinary Tuesday, not a holiday or the day before one. A parking sign
permits at most two hours during black unbracketed 09–18. You arrive at 10:00. The two-hour
restriction applies; check the other conditions before leaving the car.
scenario_pages.154:
KörkortGo · M05-L03
M05-L03
Choose a lawful place to stop
Your goal: Distinguish stopping from parking and interpret the rules, signs and time panels
for a proposed place.
Parking is leaving a vehicle stationary for a reason other than traffic conditions, avoiding danger,
boarding or alighting, or loading or unloading goods. Remaining behind the wheel does not
automatically make waiting “stopping.” Nor does switching on hazard lights create permission.
Transportstyrelsen: stopping and parking
Stopping or parking restrictions
Compare no parking with no stopping and parking. An extent marking needs its actual accompanying restriction; it
does not create permission.
C35 · No parking
Förbud mot att parkera fordon
Parking is prohibited on the signed side for the applicable
extent. This does not make stopping lawful where another rule
prohibits it. Single red diagonal across a blue circle.
Transportstyrelsen · official description
C39 · No stopping or parking
Förbud mot att stanna och parkera fordon
Both stopping and parking are prohibited for the indicated
extent. Waiting with the engine running is not a general
exemption. Red cross on a blue circle.
Transportstyrelsen · official description
scenario_pages.155:
KörkortGo · M05-L03 · Continued
Continue the learning
M21 · No stopping or parking edge marking
Förbud mot att stanna och parkera
The continuous yellow edge marking indicates a stopping and
parking prohibition. Continuous yellow line at the road edge.
Transportstyrelsen · official description
M22 · No parking edge marking
Förbud mot att parkera
The broken yellow edge marking indicates a parking
prohibition; it can also show the extent of a bus stop. Broken
yellow line at the road edge.
Transportstyrelsen · official description
M23 · Reinforcement of a stopping or parking restriction
Förbud mot att stanna och parkera eller att parkera
This yellow marking reinforces the applicable M21 or M22
restriction. Identify which prohibition applies. Yellow zigzag
marking reinforcing a stopping or parking restriction.
Transportstyrelsen · official description
Core requirements. Do not stop or park where you create danger, unnecessarily obstruct traffic
or hide a sign or signal. Normally use the right side in your direction of travel; one-way roads and
specified rail-track situations have exceptions. Secure the vehicle against rolling and prevent
unauthorised use. Open doors only without danger or unnecessary inconvenience. Traffic
Regulation, chapter 3 §§47, 50 and 52
scenario_pages.157:
KörkortGo · M05-L03 · Official examples
Other parking instructions
Keep starts and ends paired by type. C45’s 8–18 and E30’s 30-minute conditions are separate examples, not the
Tuesday two-hour exercise.
Date-based parking restrictions
C36 · No parking on odd-numbered dates
Förbud mot att parkera fordon på dag med udda datum
The parking prohibition applies on dates with an odd number.
Read the time and extent qualifications as well. Single upright
stroke on the no-parking symbol: odd-numbered dates.
Transportstyrelsen · official description
C37 · No parking on even-numbered dates
Förbud mot att parkera fordon på dag med jämnt datum
The parking prohibition applies on dates with an even
number. Read the time and extent qualifications as well. Two
upright strokes on the no-parking symbol: even-numbered
dates.
Transportstyrelsen · official description
C38 · Date-dependent parking prohibition
Datumparkering
On even dates, do not park on the side with even address
numbers; on odd dates, do not park on the odd-numbered
side. Check any time conditions. Odd/even-date symbols
divided by a red diagonal.
Transportstyrelsen · official description
scenario_pages.161:
KörkortGo · M05-L03 · Continued
Continue the learning

Förbud mot att parkera
The broken yellow edge marking indicates a parking
prohibition; it can also show the extent of a bus stop. Broken
yellow line at the road edge.
Transportstyrelsen · official description
Read the whole parking instruction. On a T6 time panel, ordinary black/white times without
brackets mean weekdays other than the day before a Sunday or public holiday; bracketed times
mean those preceding days; red times mean Sundays and public holidays. A named day applies
to that day. Check the actual date, fee, duration, vehicle group and any permit condition. A
disabled-parking permit has defined benefits, not unrestricted permission to stop anywhere.
Road Signs Regulation, T6–T8 and T16–T19 · Parking permits
Read each parking condition
Individual reference panels, not one sign assembly. T6 and T17 contain sample times that differ from the 09–18
worked example. Do not transfer their conditions to that exercise.
E19 · Parking
Parkering
Parking is permitted subject to the sign's extent, panels and
other applicable restrictions. The sign does not automatically
cancel general stopping and parking prohibitions. White P on
blue.
Transportstyrelsen · official description
scenario_pages.162:
KörkortGo · M05-L03 · Continued
Continue the learning
T6 · Time qualification
Tidsangivelse
Unbracketed black/white times apply on weekdays other than the day before a Sunday or public holiday; brackets
mean those preceding days; red means Sundays and public holidays. A named day governs regardless of its
category. A period crossing midnight continues into the next day.
Transportstyrelsen · official description
T7 · Accessible-parking permit holders
Rörelsehindrade
Below E19, the parking instruction applies to users entitled to
park with the specified accessible-parking permit. Read any
time limits too. White wheelchair symbol on blue.
